o: Sir Henryk Baskerville i doktor Mortimer byli gotowi do drogi i w dniu oznaczonym wyruszyliśmy do Devonshire.
t: Sir Henry Baskerville and Dr. Mortimer were ready for the journey, and on the appointed day we set out for Devonshire.

o: Sherlock Holmes odwiózł mnie na dworzec i udzielił ostatnich rad i wskazówek.
t: Sherlock Holmes drove me to the station and gave me his final advice and instructions.

o: — Nie będę bałamucił twego własnego sądu, poddając ci moje podejrzenia — mówił.

t: "I wish to know everything that happens, even if it seems to have no bearing on our case; above all, I want to know young Baskerville's relations with his neighbours, and every detail bearing on the death of Sir Charles."

t: One thing seems to me certain, namely that Mr. James Desmond, the nearest heir, is a man of no self-interest, and that he was not the murderer.

o: Podróż była przyjemna; czas zeszedł mi na zawiązywaniu bliższej znajomości z moimi towarzyszami i na bawieniu się z pieskiem doktora Mortimera.
t: The journey was pleasant; the time passed for me in getting better acquainted with my companions and in playing with Dr. Mortimer's little dog.

t: — One has only to look at Sir Henry's round head to see that he is of Celtic descent, and the Celts have an innate enthusiasm and capacity for attaching themselves to people and country.

t: Besides, I do not know the mansion; we lived in a secluded manor house on the south coast.

o: Stamtąd pojechałem wprost do Ameryki.
t: From there I went straight to America.

o: Cały ten kraj jest dla mnie tak obcy i nowy, jak dla doktora Watsona, a chciałbym już jak najprędzej zobaczyć łąkę i przyległe trzęsawisko.
t: The whole country is as foreign and new to me as it is to Dr. Watson, and I should like to see the moor and the adjacent fen as soon as possible.

o: — Pańskie życzenie już się spełniło.
t: "Your wish is already fulfilled.

t: In his drawn brows and the set of his mouth one could read an indomitable will and energy.

t: Our arrival was evidently the event of the day, for porters thronged around us, and the station master with his staff watched us curiously.

t: We took our seats in the vehicle, and the horses sped off quickly; we passed neat farms surrounded by gardens, but in the distance the moor still lay grey and barren.

t: He was jailed for murder in Notting Hill.

t: His death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment: he was declared insane; the judges could not believe that he had committed so monstrous a crime while being in his right mind.

t: The fertile countryside lay behind us; before us stretched grey, barren land, with a human habitation appearing only rarely, ringed about by a stone wall.

t: A few minutes later we were already passing through the palace gate, ancient and vaulted; a moment later the mansion revealed itself to us, rebuilt with South African gold by Sir Charles.

t: The two of us were enough for Sir Charles, but Your Lordship will surely want to live in a more courtly fashion, receive guests, and will need more servants.

t: "Well, what do you intend to do?"

t: That part of the house had evidently been rebuilt; the rooms were bright, furnished in modern fashion, and equipped with every comfort.

t: In a moment we went down to the dining hall.

o: Była to komnata wysoka, staroświecka, przedzielona na dwie części: w jednej, do której wchodziło się po trzech schodkach, za dawnych czasów jadali suzerenowie, zaś w niższej — wasale.
t: It was a lofty, old-fashioned hall divided into two parts: in the upper one, reached by three steps, the suzerains used to dine in days of yore, while in the lower one the vassals sat.

o: Sklepione sufity nadawały jeszcze powagi tej komnacie, która przy świetle pochodni, wśród gwaru uczty, bywała nieraz jasna i wesoła, ale teraz, w blasku lampy przyświecającej dwom gentlemanom we frakach, wydawała się anachronizmem.
t: The vaulted ceilings lent the room yet more dignity; by torchlight, amid the din of the feast, it was sometimes bright and cheerful, but now, in the glow of a lamp shining on two gentlemen in dress coats, it seemed an anachronism.

o: Wszystkie cztery ściany były ozdobione wizerunkami przodków, poczynając od rycerzy z czasów Elżbiety, a kończąc na przedostatnim właścicielu Baskerville Hall.
t: All four walls were adorned with portraits of the ancestors, beginning with the knights of Elizabeth's time and ending with the penultimate owner of Baskerville Hall.

o: Mówiliśmy mało i przyznam, że byłem rad, gdy obiad skończył się i mogliśmy wyjść do bilardowego pokoju na cygaro.
t: We spoke little, and I confess I was glad when dinner was over and we could go out to the billiard room for a cigar.

o: — Niezbyt wesoła rezydencja…
t: "Not a very cheerful residence..."

o: — rzekł sir Henryk.
t: "..." said Sir Henry.

o: — Przypuszczam, że można się do niej przyzwyczaić, ale na razie czuję się nieswojo.
t: "I suppose one can get used to it, but for the present I feel uneasy."

o: Nic dziwnego, że mój stryj stał się dziwakiem.
t: No wonder that my uncle has become an eccentric.

o: Połóżmy się wcześniej.
t: Let us go to bed early.

o: Może jutro, przy blasku słonecznym te komnaty przedstawią nam się weselej.
t: Perhaps tomorrow, in the sunlight, these rooms will present a gayer aspect to us.

o: Przed udaniem się na spoczynek podniosłem roletę i wyjrzałem przez okno.
t: Before retiring for the night I raised the blind and looked out through the window.

o: Widok był na trawnik przed portykiem.
t: The view was onto the lawn in front of the portico.

o: Pośrodku stały dwa dęby miotane wiatrem.
t: In the middle stood two oaks, tossed by the wind.

o: Księżyc, w ostatniej kwadrze, przeświecał blado przez chmury.
t: The moon, in its last quarter, shone pale through the clouds.

o: Z dala widniały nagie skały, a poza nimi trzęsawisko.
t: In the distance bare rocks could be seen, and beyond them the moor.

o: Spuściłem roletę, nie chcąc patrzeć dłużej na ten ponury krajobraz.
t: I let down the blind, not wishing to look longer upon that gloomy landscape.

o: Byłem zmęczony, a jednak usnąć nie mogłem; obracałem się z boku na bok.
t: I was tired, yet I could not sleep; I turned from side to side.

o: Na dole zegar wybijał kwadranse, poza tym panowała cisza grobowa.
t: Below, the clock struck the quarter hours, and beyond that there was a deathly silence.

o: Nagle przerwał ją płacz niewieści.
t: Suddenly it was broken by the cry of a woman.

o: Usiadłem na łóżku i począłem nasłuchiwać.
t: I sat down on the bed and began to listen.

o: Przez pół godziny czekałem w natężeniu, ale oprócz płaczu nie usłyszałem nic zgoła.
t: For half an hour I listened intently, but apart from the crying I heard nothing at all.
